title: Align PRD with KV-cache & cold-start safeguards: concrete requirements, gating, and acceptance tests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: After the February KV-cache+cold-start outage (link below) the SRE and runtime teams produced a postmortem with 8 action items. This ticket translates those action items into concrete PRD requirements, acceptance tests, and release gating so product and engineering have a single source of truth for implementation and verification.

Background: The incident exposed two classes of failures: (1) KV-cache regeneration latency during heavy prefix churn that caused request queuing and increased tail latency; (2) cold-start autoscale behaviour where warm-pool sizing and burst policies did not meet the real traffic pattern, causing high error rate for low-latency SLO customers. The postmortem recommends runtime changes, additional telemetry, and deployment constraints.

Goals: 1) Convert postmortem action items into measurable PRD requirements; 2) Define canary and rollout gating criteria tied to SLO-sensitive metrics; 3) Define acceptance tests and synthetic checks to prevent regressions; 4) Ensure operational runbook updates and on-call playbooks are captured in release exit criteria.

Non-goals: This ticket does not specify exact kernel-level optimizations or GPU fallback code paths; those remain in ENG implementation tickets. It also does not rework billing or tenant-level quotas.

Proposed requirements (high level): 1) Runtime must expose a KV-cache regen metric with percentile latency (p50/p95/p99) and regen-rate per-minute per-model; 2) Autoscale cold-start warm-pool default for Dedicated must be conservative for low-latency customers and configurable per-customer; 3) The platform must provide an automated canary policy that evaluates both latency SLOs and regen-failure counts before promoting a release; 4) A synthetic suite that simulates prefix churn + traffic spike must pass in CI with thresholds; 5) The Console must show a per-route "KV Cache Health" score (green/amber/red) and recommended mitigations.

Implementation constraints and trade-offs: - Tightening warm-pool sizes reduces cost efficiency; product must balance revenue risk vs SLO exposure. Recommend a tiered default: free/self-serve customers keep current defaults; Dedicated and Private customers default to higher warm-pool until they opt out. - Adding dense telemetry increases cardinality and storage cost. We'll phase metrics: critical regen metrics retained at high resolution; debug-level events sampled. - Canary gates add release latency; to mitigate, allow parallel canary lanes and automated rollback to an approved fallback (e.g., lower concurrency model variant).

Runbook and operations: Update runbook to include steps for forced KV-cache regen, cache-size inspection, and automated cache warm-up. Define on-call checklist for cache-regeneration alerts and a step to enable degraded-serving fallback.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field for discrete items.

Rollout plan: 1) Design spec and telemetry schema (2 sprints) 2) Implement metrics + Console UI + canary policy (3 sprints) 3) Integrate synthetic CI checks and runbook updates (1 sprint) 4) Beta rollout to Dedicated customers, monitor for 2 weeks, then gradual hosted rollout.

Metrics & monitoring: Primary metrics to gate on canary and release: p99 latency (route-level), error-rate spikes (>1% relative increase), KV-cache regen p95 latency, KV-cache failure count per minute, synthetic-scenario pass rate. Define guardrail thresholds in a separate artifact.

Links and artifacts: see links field.

Owner responsibilities: PM (Aisha) owns PRD updates and rollouts; ENG leads (Lucas) owns implementation and metric instrumentation; SRE owns runbook and SLO verification.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument KV-cache regen metric with tags: model, region, route, and expose p50/p95/p99 latency and failures_per_minute
Define Console "KV Cache Health" widget and a public guideline page with remediation steps
Add a synthetic CI scenario that simulates prefix churn + 3x traffic spike; pipeline must report pass/fail and block merge on failure for runtime-1.20 releases
Create canary gating policy that requires: no >10% relative increase in p99 latency, <0.5% absolute error-rate increase, KV-cache failure rate within baseline for 48h before full rollout
Provide a warm-pool sizing default table per customer tier and an API flag to override for Dedicated/Private customers
Update operational runbook with step-by-step KVs regen remedy, runbook snippet included in release notes
Proof of concept staged rollout executed on two Dedicated customers with telemetry dashboards and no regression to existing SLOs for 14 days
